exchange_rates.note: Fixed demo rates — do not call live API

EXW.note: Highest risk — buyer pays pickup from factory gate plus all downstream costs

standard_freight_rates_sea_to_los_angele.note: Per unit, standard ocean freight. Air freight adds ~5x.

duty_rates_by_part_family.note: US import duty rates. Source: HTSUS. Rates subject to change. Section 301 China tariffs may apply — check current status.

DT_drivetrain.note: Most drivetrain parts duty-free under HS 8714

BR_brakes.note: Bicycle brake parts duty-free — NOT 2.6% (misclassification correction)

insurance_note: 0.5% of (unit_price + freight + duty). Apply only for FOB or EXW incoterms.

landed_cost_formula.step_1: Convert quote to USD using exchange_rates above
landed_cost_formula.step_2: If incoterm is FOB or EXW: add freight_cost_usd from parts_sourcing_meta.json
landed_cost_formula.step_3: If incoterm is FOB, CIF, or EXW: apply duty = (usd_price + freight) * duty_rate_pct
landed_cost_formula.step_4: If incoterm is FOB or EXW: apply insurance = (usd_price + freight + duty) * 0.005
landed_cost_formula.step_5: Apply volume-adjusted unit price from moq_price_breaks in parts_sourcing_meta.json
landed_cost_formula.formula: landed_cost = volume_adjusted_price + freight + duty + insurance + moq_surcharge

moq_surcharge_rule.note: 15% added to base unit price when ordering below MOQ. Covers supplier setup and handling.

corrected_critical_path.note: Day numbers below are RELATIVE INBOUND SEQUENCING — the order in which parts arrive at facility once all are en route. Absolute lead times from PO are 10-50 days depending on supplier and model — see assembly_estimates.json for per-model actual lead times.

arrival_sequence_at_facility.why: Frame is always the longest lead-time item; assembly cannot start until frame arrives

corrected_assembly_duration_hours_per_bi.wrong_value_in_prior_doc: 45-60 minutes is only achievable in a >50,000 unit/year fully automated factory — not applicable to D2C batch production

sourcing_decision_rules: 1. ALWAYS read frame supplier lead time first — this is the critical path anchor for every model
2. Suspension fork (MTB only) has longer lead than frame — AlpineShox 45d vs frame 35d. Fork is the true MTB critical path
3. Prefer DDP quotes (no surprises). CIF is next best. FOB requires careful landed cost calc. Never underestimate EXW.
4. DO NOT add freight to CIF or DDP quotes — it is already included
5. DO NOT skip duty on FOB quotes — it is a real buyer cost
6. If order_qty < MOQ: add 15% surcharge. Do not pretend you can order below MOQ without penalty
7. Volume discount breakpoints are real — if you need 6,000 units and the break is at 5,000, always hit it
8. A supplier 3% cheaper but 15 days slower on a critical-path part is NOT the right choice — defer to lead-time specialist
9. Single-source parts (frames, suspension forks) have no cost optimization levers — focus optimization on commodity parts
10. Currency quotes: always convert to USD using fixed rates above before comparing suppliers
